title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: handle client cancel, disconnect/reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Streaming clients (OpenAI-compat and native SDKs) observe flakiness when clients abort mid-stream, or when TCP disconnects occur then clients reconnect. This causes token duplication, leaked KV cache entries, and requests stuck on server-side timeouts. This PR implements a unified streaming lifecycle control surface to handle: client cancel events, abrupt disconnect detection, reconnect/resume semantics, and server-side idle/response timeouts. Motivation: make streaming stable for long-running generations, function/tool calling flows, and structured-output streams without requiring app teams to implement fragile client-side heuristics. Changes: 1) Add explicit lifecycle signals in the streaming protocol (SSE and WebSocket): CANCEL, CLIENT_DISCONNECT, RESUME_SESSION. 2) Server-side session manager persists short-lived streaming sessions (default 60s) keyed by session_id; on disconnect the runtime trims in-progress KV cache but keeps session state to allow resume. 3) Implement resume tokens and resume_offset to safely continue generation without token duplication; resume verifies generation checksum and replays missing tokens if needed. 4) Implement server timeouts: idle_timeout (default 30s) for paused sessions and hard_timeout (configurable per-route) to abort long-running generations and emit structured final events for OpenAI-compat clients. 5) Integrate with OpenAI-compat streaming layer: preserve SSE event semantics (data: [DONE]) and add compat headers for session resume. 6) Update function/tool-calling flow to treat CANCEL as a cancel of the active tool call and to surface a structured error payload to callers. 7) Add end-to-end tests and integration flakiness regression tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement protocol signals and server handlers - [x] Add session manager with in-memory + optional redis backing (config flag) - [x] Implement resume token verification & offset logic - [x] Add timeouts and graceful abort paths - [x] Update OpenAI-compat streaming code path - [x] Update SDK compatibility points (python/ts) - [x] Add e2e tests and unit tests - [x] Update docs: docs/api/streaming.md and openai_compat notes Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for short-lived connections; resume is opt-in via session_id/Resume-Token header. See ENG-1245 for rollout plan.
commits: Add lifecycle protocol signals and session manager (streaming/lifecycle.go)
Hook resume tokens into openai_compat streaming handler
Add timeouts and abort paths with tests
Fix race on kv cache cleanup (runtime/kvcache.go)
Address review feedback: tighten resume token entropy and add extra checks
review_comments: Samir Patel: Overall looks good; two concerns: 1) race when session expires while client reconnects, 2) perf impact when resume state kept for many sessions. Suggest adding metrics and a configurable expiry TTL.
Ava Chen: Addressed by adding streaming.session.expire metric and redis-backed optional store. Session TTL default is 60s, configurable per-route. Added unit tests for race case.
Lena Rodriguez: Please ensure OpenAI-compat SSE preserves exact event ordering and [DONE] behavior; also please call out that function/tool calls will receive a structured cancel payload.
Ava Chen: Confirmed ordering preserved; added compatibility test in tests/streaming/test_openai_compat_resume.py. Function cancel payload shape documented in docs/api/streaming.md.
Priya Nair: LGTM after small nits. Please squash commits and add release notes.

release_notes:
- Streaming: add lifecycle controls (CANCEL, CLIENT_DISCONNECT, RESUME_SESSION) with session resume tokens and server timeouts.
- OpenAI-compat: resume support and structured cancel payloads for function/tool calls.
- Config: session TTL, idle_timeout, hard_timeout per-route.
- Metrics: streaming.session.resume, streaming.session.expire.
